channel.title: Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs
channel.description: This is the website of the Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs Working group (SWG) of the Innovation Center for Agricultural System Transformation (IAT) as part of the Leibniz Centre for Agricultural Landscape Research (ZALF).

item.title: DML Presents its Services at the IAT Statusseminar 2026
item.description:
On 24 September we opened the afternoon session of the IAT Statusseminar 2026, held at Justus Liebig University Giessen, with an overview of the services offered by the Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs (DML) working group. Six months after we first introduced our service concept at the IAT kickoff, this was a chance to show what that concept looks like in practice.

The talk was structured around the three strata of our service concept, each illustrated with projects we have completed or are working on with colleagues across the IAT:

  • Support: helping researchers manage their data and software across every stage of a project. Examples included the IAT Data Management and Protection handbook, research software such as BirdNET-Passage, the Living Lab workshop maps, our Quarto workshop and the IAT ZALF templates.
  • Transfer: closing the loop between science and practice, with project websites and the Living Lab Explorer, a dashboard co-designed with the IAT Regional Network Managers.
  • Integration: connecting research data and methods across the IAT, through the IAT Project Tracker, a common data management plan template and the how-to guide for Policy Labs.

During the talk we also asked the audience a series of live questions, from what happens to research data once a project ends to which training formats work best. Thank you to everyone who took part: your answers will help us shape our training and support offer for the coming year.

item.title: Upcoming Quarto Workshop at iEMSs 2026
item.description:
We are excited to announce that the DML group will host a workshop at the International Environmental Modelling and Software Society (iEMSs) 2026 conference in Dublin over the 12-16th July.

The workshop “One Publishing Tool to Rule Them All: Quarto for Documentation, Presentations, Manuscripts and Outreach”, which is being prepared in collaboration with researchers from ETH Zurich will explore Quarto as a unified solution for academic communication. Quarto can generate multiple output formats — PDF, HTML, LaTeX, and DOCX — from a single source document while supporting executable code in Python, R, Julia, and Observable. Through short presentations and guided exercises, participants will learn to produce documentation, reproducible journal articles, presentations, outreach websites, and interactive dashboards — all from one tool.

We will make the content from both the workshop available online prior to the conference, so stay tuned for more updates!

item.title: DML at Barcamp Open Science 2026
item.description:
On 10 June we joined the 12th Barcamp Open Science at Wikimedia Deutschland in Berlin, together with around 45 other participants from research institutions, libraries and infrastructure projects. This year the event ran under the heading of navigating challenging times, in recognition of the growing political and geopolitical pressure on open research practices.

A barcamp is an un-conference: the agenda is not fixed in advance, and participants propose and lead the sessions themselves. In practice this means far more discussion than presentation, which suits a topic like Open Science where practice differs so much between institutions and disciplines.

We proposed and moderated a session on effective “carrot and stick” approaches to incentivising Open Science in different institutional contexts. The discussion was honest about how little the current incentives achieve. Career benefits that are promised for open practices rarely materialise, and funder mandates such as data management plans are often not checked for compliance. Participants also described a reluctance to publish data out of concern that imperfections would become visible. The conclusion was that both carrots and sticks are still needed, but that neither will work without a broader cultural shift — including, in the spirit of George Box, accepting that all data are imperfect but some data are useful.

Other sessions covered the role of open research in supporting democratic values, the attribution of AI-generated data, and open educational resources. The organising team has now published a wrap-up of the whole event, which DML contributed to: Barcamp Open Science 2026: Navigating Challenging Times.

We would like to thank the organising team from the Leibniz Strategy Forum Open Science and Wikimedia Deutschland for hosting, and we would recommend the barcamp format to anyone at IAT or in the Living Labs whose work touches on Open Science. We are looking forward to the next one.

Photos from Barcamp Open Science 2026, attribution: Ralf Rebmann 2026.

item.title: DML Presents at IAT Kickoff Meeting
item.description: In March 2026 the Innovation Center for Agricultural System Transformation (IAT) was officially launched, with two days of events at the Futurium in Berlin as well as the ZALF campus in Müncheberg. The focus of the 2nd day was on connecting researchers working on similar topics within the IAT from both ZALF and the partner institutions. We were fortunate to have an opportunity to present our concept for how the Data and Modelling Infrastructure for Living Labs group (DML) will provide a three pillar approach of services to support IAT researchers and living labs in their data and modelling needs. The slides we presented are available below, and we are looking forward to engaging with the IAT and broader ZALF community in the coming months to produce some real outputs from collaborations to serve as a showcase for the services we can provide.

item.title: DML at the FAIRagro Community Summit
item.description:
In March, DML working group members travelled to Frankfurt to attend the FAIRagro Community Summit. The event brought together the FAIRagro community to showcase the services and tools the consortium has been developing to advance Open and FAIR data practices in agricultural research.

FAIRagro is an NFDI consortium that has represented the agrosystems research community in Germany since 2023. With more than 30 partners, it is building a FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) research data management infrastructure — developing the tools and workflows needed to support Open Science and sustainable crop production.

The summit was a great opportunity to exchange ideas, hear about ongoing developments, and connect with others working on research data challenges in agriculture. We look forward to future collaboration with the FAIRagro consortium!
